newsitem.title: HONG KONG: BA to expand Hong Kong service.
newsitem.headline: BA to expand Hong Kong service.

text.p: British Airways is planning to offer more flights between Hong Kong and London and wants to start a new service to Shanghai "as soon as possible," said chief executive Robert Ayling.

"We want to expand by operating more services. We think there will be more growth in the market between the UK, Europe and Hong Kong," Ayling told reporters in Hong Kong. His visit is part of a tour of BA's principal destinations with the theme 'Taking British Airways into the new millenium.'

"We want to develop our services in the Chinese market and our commitment to serve Hong Kong is as resolute as it has ever been. We want to be the principal carrier in this developing market place - bringing services here is what we are talking about. We think there will be growth in the Hong Kong-London sector of maybe six percent over the next three years," he added.

But availability of slots at BA's Heathrow home is the main problem which will have to be overcome before the additional flights can begin, Ayling said. They may be able to start before the scheduled opening of Hong Kong's new airport in April 1998, he added.

BA says its twice-daily flights between London and Hong Kong is its third largest revenue earning destination after New York and Tokyo enjoying 48 per cent of the total market after Cathay Pacific (35 percent) and Virgin Atlantic (17 percent).
Ayling said he is awaiting Chinese government approval before flights to Shanghai can start "in the forseeable future".
BA's rivals Virgin Atlantic also said recently it wanted to start a Shanghai service. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
